key_insight: T2D-Bench tests whether LLM diabetes advice is not just fluent, but explicitly backed by computable evidence paths tied to guidelines and lifestyle effects.
clinical_relevance: This framework could help surface unsupported or omitted diabetes-care recommendations before LLM outputs are used in patient-facing or clinician-support settings.
method: Built a multi-layer knowledge graph combining UMLS, DrugBank, SIDER, ADA guideline rules, and lifestyle-to-glycemia links.
Evaluated 100 structured vignettes covering diagnosis, medication safety, and conflicting lifestyle scenarios.
Applied an evidence gate plus constrained revision to check and repair outputs against benchmark-defined evidence requirements.
evidence_signal: Across 100 vignettes, baseline outputs failed evidence-path checks in 35% of GPT-4o-mini cases and 33% of GPT-4o cases.
watch_item: The benchmark depends on graph coverage and rule encoding, so gaps in the knowledge graph or guideline formalization could miss valid context or over-restrict responses.
paper_title: T2D-Bench: Evidence-Gated Evaluation of LLM Outputs for Type 2 Diabetes Using a Multi-Layer Clinical-Lifestyle Knowledge Graph
